answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by requiring every identity to lock a stake bond before it may earn. The bond sits untouched while the agent works honestly, but if peers prove the identity is a copy, the bond is slashed and the fake ends at once. Like an ivory seal that only opens to those who post collateral, a single whisper of proven fraud costs the forger real money: minting a thousand fakes means locking a thousand bonds, so each pigment of fake identity is priced in advance while honest agents risk only what they can afford to lose.
